content.user_title: Improve Google SEO with Official Guidance
content.value_statement: SEO work fails when teams rely on outdated advice. This skill applies Google Search documentation to audits, fixes, and content planning.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes official Google Search guidance for crawling, indexing, serving, and ranking topics.
Explains Search Console reports and monitoring steps for developers and marketers.
Guides structured data planning for videos, breadcrumbs, snippets, and rich results.
Reviews technical SEO issues such as canonical URLs, robots rules, hreflang, and mobile-first indexing.
Provides practical checklists for site audits, migrations, content quality, and link practices.
limitations: It does not guarantee ranking improvements or traffic increases.
It cannot access private Search Console data unless the user provides it.
It may need current Google documentation checks for recent policy changes.
It does not replace legal, security, or accessibility review.

use_cases.title: Audit a Product Site
use_cases.description: Review search appearance, structured data, crawlability, and indexing signals against official Google guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan Technical Fixes
use_cases.description: Prioritize fixes for canonical URLs, robots rules, JavaScript rendering, hreflang, and mobile-first indexing.

use_cases.title: Prepare Content Briefs
use_cases.description: Create content requirements for titles, snippets, links, helpful content, and rich result eligibility.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic SEO
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one page or page type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page for basic Google SEO issues. Focus on titles, descriptions, headings, links, images, and crawlability.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Indexing Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose why these URLs are crawled but not indexed. Use official Google guidance and list likely causes first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Structured Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for rich result eligibility.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend structured data for this content type. Include required properties, validation steps, and common mistakes to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Technical SEO Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across a large site.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a prioritized technical SEO plan for this site migration. Cover crawling, canonicalization, redirects, hreflang, mobile parity, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: A team asks why important pages are discovered but not indexed.
output: Check whether pages return successful status codes and meaningful content.
Review canonical signals, duplicate content, robots rules, and noindex directives.
Use Search Console examples to separate crawl access issues from quality or duplication issues.

output_examples.input: A publisher wants richer video results in Google Search.
output: Identify the right video structured data fields for the page type.
Confirm that video URLs, thumbnails, titles, and publication dates are visible and consistent.
Validate the page with Google tools before release.

output_examples.input: A developer is planning an international site launch.
output: Map each language and regional URL pair before implementation.
Check canonical and alternate signals together, not separately.
Monitor indexing and search performance after launch.

best_practices: Provide the site type, affected URLs, target countries, and current Search Console symptoms.
Ask for a prioritized plan when many SEO issues appear at the same time.
Validate generated recommendations against live pages and current Google documentation before release.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for guaranteed ranking improvements or traffic promises.
Do not use the skill to justify spam tactics, cloaking, hidden text, or paid link schemes.
Do not copy sample markup without replacing placeholder URLs and required page-specific values.

faq.question: Does this skill use official Google guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It is organized around Google Search documentation about SEO, crawling, indexing, Search Console, and rich results.

faq.question: Can it guarantee better rankings?
faq.answer: No. It can help improve compliance and quality signals, but Google ranking depends on many factors.

faq.question: Can it review Search Console reports?
faq.answer: Yes, if you provide report details, exported data, or specific messages from Search Console.

faq.question: Is it useful for developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers technical topics such as rendering, robots rules, canonical URLs, redirects, and structured data.

faq.question: Can it create structured data guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain suitable structured data types, required fields, validation steps, and common implementation mistakes.

faq.question: Should recommendations be checked before publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. Validate changes on real pages and confirm recent Google documentation for policy-sensitive topics.
